He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State Bulldogs]] and the [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M Aggies]]. ==Early life and high school career== Andersson Garcia was born on August 23, 2000, in [[Moca, Dominican Republic]].{{cite web |title=Andersson Garcia |url=https://gleague.nba.com/player/1643158/andersson-garcia |website=[[NBA G League]] |access-date=12 March 2026 |language=en}} As a child in the Dominican Republic, he played [[baseball]] more than any other sport, but stopped playing after growing afraid of fast [[pitch (baseball)|pitches]].{{cite web |last1=Coleman |first1=Joel |title=Why Not? The Story Of Andersson Garcia |url=https://hailstate.com/news/2022/1/17/mens-basketball-why-not-the-story-of-andersson-garcia-coleman |website=[[Mississippi State University|Mississippi State Athletics]] |access-date=12 March 2026 |language=en |date=17 January 2022}} He started playing basketball at age 11 when a coach invited him to play in a tournament. After being scouted at a basketball camp in the Dominican Republic, Garcia attended Hamilton Heights Christian Academy in [[Chattanooga, Tennessee]]. ==College career== Garcia signed with the [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State Bulldogs]] after developing a bond with assistant coach Korey McCray. On May 13, 2022, Garcia signed with the [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M Aggies]].{{cite web |last1=Roberts |first1=Evan |title=Aggies Ink Andersson Garcia |url=https://12thman.com/news/2022/5/12/mens-basketball-aggies-ink-andersson-garcia |website=[[Texas A&M]] |access-date=12 March 2026 |language=en |date=13 May 2022}} In the 2023–24 season, Garcia was the only Power Five player to reach 300 rebounds, 200 points, 50 assists, 40 steals, and 20 blocks in the season. He holds the Texas A&M record for most rebounds in a season, and was granted the nickname "Dominican [[Dennis Rodman]]" by his then-coach [[Buzz Williams]]. ==Professional career== In 2025, Garcia joined the [[Marineros de Puerto Plata]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto]], the top professional basketball league in the [[Dominican Republic]].{{cite web |last1=Burton |first1=DJ |title=Texas A&M Aggies Star Dominating in Next Chapter of Career |url=https://www.si.com/college/tamu/basketball/texas-am-aggies-andersson-garcia-dominating-next-chapter-career |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=12 March 2026 |date=30 May 2025}} In the 2025 season, the league named him Rookie of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Johnson |first1=Jarrett |title=Former Texas A&M basketball star named DRNBL Rookie of the Year |url=https://aggieswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/aggies/mens-basketball/2025/07/22/texas-aggies-basketball-andersson-garcia-crowned-rookie-of-the-year-in-drnbl/85332029007/ |website=[[USA Today]] |access-date=12 March 2026 |date=22 July 2025}} Following his success on the Marineros de Puerto Plata, Garcia was signed to the [[Mexico City Capitanes]] of the [[NBA G League]] for the [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–26 season]], where he played alongside former Texas A&M teammate [[Wade Taylor IV]].{{cite web |last1=Johnson |first1=Jarrett |title=Texas A&M’s Andersson Garcia finding success in the G League |url=https://aggieswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/aggies/mens-basketball/2026/01/16/texas-aggies-football-andersson-garcia-pro-career/88203575007/ |website=[[USA Today]] |access-date=12 March 2026 |date=16 January 2026}} On March 11, 2026, the [[Utah Jazz]] signed Garcia to a 10-day contract.{{cite web |title=Utah Jazz Sign Andersson Garcia to 10-Day Contract {{!}} Utah Jazz |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-andersson-garcia-to-10-day-contract |website=[[NBA]] |access-date=12 March 2026 |language=en |date=11 March 2026}} On March 15, Garcia made his first career start, recording three points, 11 rebounds, three assists, and two steals in a 111–116 loss to the [[2025–26 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]].{{Cite web|title=Jazz's Andersson Garcia: Pulls down 11 boards in start|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-andersson-garcia-pulls-down-11-boards-in-start/|access-date=May 29, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} On July 14, 2026, Garcia signed with [[CB Breogán|Río Breogán]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite web|title=El Río Breogán incorpora al ala-pívot dominicano Andersson García|url=https://www.acb.com/es/liga/noticias/el-rio-breogan-incorpora-al-ala-pivot-dominicano-andersson-garcia-145580|date=July 14, 2026|access-date=July 14, 2026|website=acb.com|language=es}}
